source_text: Quoniam ergo permisit et permittendo uoluit spiritus sanctus ordinem ipsius muneris conscribi, etsi indigni ad supplementum tantae gloriae describendae, tamen quasi mandatum sanctissimae Perpetuae, immo fideicommissum eius exequimur, unum adicientes documentum de ipsius constantia et animi sublimitate. Cum a tribuno castigatius eo tractantur, quia ex admonitionibus hominum uanissimorum uerebatur ne subtraherentur de carcere incantationibus aliquibus magicis, in faciem ei respondit: Quid utique non permittis nobis refrigerare noxiis nobilissimis, Caesaris scilicet natali depugnaturis? Aut non tua gloria est, si pinguiores illo producamur? Horruit et erubuit tribunus; et ita iussit illos humanius haberi, ut et fratribus eius et ceteris facultas fieret introeundi et refrigerandi cum eis, iam et ipso optione carceris credente.
thought_title: Perpetua rebukes the tribune and wins relief
orientation: The redactor is now speaking after Felicity has given birth, adding one more deed before the public games.
pass_a_gloss: Since therefore the Holy Spirit permitted and by permitting willed that the order of that same public games be written down, although we are unworthy for the supplement of so great glory to be described, nevertheless as if it were the command of most holy Perpetua, indeed her entrusted charge, we carry it out, adding one proof of her constancy and loftiness of mind. When they were treated rather harshly by the tribune, because from the warnings of most vain men he was fearing lest they be stolen away from prison by some magical incantations, she answered to his face: Why then do you not permit us, most noble condemned ones, to get relief, us who are about to fight on Caesar's birthday, that is? Or is it not your glory, if we are brought out fatter on that day? The tribune shuddered and blushed; and so he ordered them to be held more humanely, so that both for her brothers and for the rest opportunity was made to enter and to get relief with them, with now even the prison adjutant himself believing.

pass_b_english: Since the Holy Spirit has permitted the record of these public games to be written down, and in permitting it has willed it, we are carrying out what stands as a command from most holy Perpetua, indeed a charge she entrusted to us, although we are unworthy to add to the telling of so great a glory. We add one further proof of her firm resolve and her greatness of mind.

The tribune had begun to treat them rather harshly because he had listened to the warnings of utterly foolish men and feared they would be stolen out of prison by some magical incantations. Perpetua answered him to his face: "Why do you not let us get relief, the most noble condemned ones who are about to fight, of course, for Caesar's birthday? Or is it not to your credit if we are brought out fatter on that day?" The tribune shuddered and blushed. Then he ordered them to be kept more humanely, so that her brothers and the others were given leave to come in and get relief with them, and by this time even the prison adjutant himself had come to believe.
notes: eo in Cum a tribuno castigatius eo tractantur is obscure in the given text; glossed as intensifier left untranslated rather than inventing a correction.
